findings.comment:

Dishes done this morning will be rewashed so that they are properly sanitized. A new dish machine is being installed tomorrow. The new machine is a temperature sanitizing machine. findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed foods in the small over/under cooler to be 50F. These foods are cut lettuce and various flavors of Smuckers jellies and toppings. The kitchen was instructed to call Smuckers to determine if the label marking, “refrigerate after opening” is for food quality or food safety.  It appears that the mark may be for quality. However, as this is a senior care facility they should check before determining weather to discard or keep these items. Some of the items are low sugar or sweetened with Splenda. Cut lettuce was discarded immediately. 3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 
This unit can be used for whole produce but nothing that requires refrigeration for safety shall be kept in this unit until it is repaired or 
replaced.

The 3 door unit along the front all is holding food between 40F and 43F. The time temperature control for safety foods were moved to the 3 door unit along the back wall and technician was called for repair. Repair or replace this unit and do not use it until it is able to maintain food at 41F or below.

(D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 An employee was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off prior to manually dispensing paper towels to dry hands. Proper technique was discussed. Employee was later observed washing hands properly by preparing paper towels to dry hands prior to beginning the process and using the paper towels as a barrier after drying hands to shut off the faucet.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink. Forearms and elbows may also be used to shut off the faucet or dispense paper towels to avoid touching handles with freshly washed hands.

 The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored

Properly store all chemicals. The cleaner was removed.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - Foods were observed with date marks indicating products were past the 7 day time frame for use. Items included ham (5/8), diet pudding (5/9), and manwich sauce (5/3). The aforementioned products were discarded in the trash during inspection.
A portion of deli meat in the bottom of the dairy cooler had a date mark of 3/20. The employee noted that was the day the product was first opened and frozen. It was placed in the cooler to thaw as of this past Sunday (5/15) and would be served tomorrow (5/18). Benefit of the doubt was given for the portion of deli meat, but date marking and tracking dates for frozen/thawing ready to eat, potentially hazardous foods were discussed.

Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly dated and used or discarded w/in 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.
NOTE: Freezing portions of foods will stop the clock on the 7 day time frame. For example, freezing deli meat opened today would mean once the product was pulled from the freezer it would have 6 days to be used or discarded after thawing. If foods are frozen, make sure date marks reflect proper time frame so the total time for use does not exceed 7 days. Keep track of dates so there is no confusion when foods are frozen and then removed from the freezer to be thawed for use.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The can opener blade was soiled with food debris, and the area around the blade had buildup of metal shavings. Can opener was placed through the dish machine prior to using for dinner prep.

To prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris, food contact surfaces must be properly clean and sanitize between uses/as needed and up to every 4hrs after continuous use for in-use food contact surfaces/equipment (i.e. can opener, cutting boards, knives, etc.).

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.citation_text:
750.100 - Three severely dents cans of olives (Musco Family Olive Company; 51oz each) were stocked in the dry storage room for use. Cans were set aside for return supplier, and labeled with a note that said "do not use; return for credit (3 cans of olives)".
Two cans of dill pickle spears were also missing labels. Manager noted labels are typically discarded if they area falling off of cans upon delivery. Manager was advised the labels need to be maintained on the cans in some form (i.e. use tape to keep labels on cans). Pickles were labeled and kept for use.

Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption. **Cans that are dented on the top, bottom or side seams, severely dented on any surface of the can, bulging, rusty, or questionable in any way must not be stocked for use. Refuse questionable products when shipments are received, when possible, and/or set aside dented cans for credit when discovered. If an intact can gets damaged in some manner during stocking, immediately open the can and store the product in a clean, covered properly labeled food grade container in the cooler.**

Food shall be obtained from sources that comply with all laws relating to food and food labeling. Maintain labels on all commercially processed foods. If a can is missing a label upon delivery and the label is not in the box, set aside the can to return to the supplier for credit**

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Sani-bucket solution (located on toaster counter) was at 0ppm chlorine. A damp disposable wiping cloth was observed on the counter next to the bucket.
Wiping cloth was discarded in the trash. 

Maintain bleach solutions for wiping surfaces at 100-200ppm. If disposable wiping cloths are no longer needed, then discard them in the trash. Otherwise, store wiping cloths in the sanitizer solution between uses until they are ready to be discarded. Change solutions every 2 to 4 hours or more often is solutions and wiping cloths become heavily soiled. Frequent use of wiping cloths will cause sanitizer solution to weaken at an accelerated rate.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - Open container of cottage cheese had date mark of 9/9/14 on the lid. Container of cottage cheese (less than 1/4 remaining) was discarded in the trash. Staff member stated it would have been discarded once she saw the old date. However, the date mark indicated the product was well beyond the 7 day time frame for use.
Dairy products (i.e. American cheese, 2% milk, skim milk, cottage cheese, half and half, etc.) must be dated once they are opened and used or discarded w/in 7 days. Day one starts the date when the seal is broken on product packaging. Cottage cheese opened on 9/9 had to be used or discarded by 9/15. Manufacturer's use by date only supersedes the date mark once the products are opened if the use by date falls prior to the 7th day of use. Cultured products, such as buttermilk, sour cream, and yogurt, are exempt from the date marking requirement.

Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours must be clearly dated and consumed or discarded w/in 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 & 1120e - Employee working in dish room was observed drying his hands on a wiping cloth that would normally be used with sani-buckets. The cloth used is a disposable item but was being used more than once to wipe hands and placed on a cart in the dish room for later use. Employee was advised on proper handwashing and use of paper towels. The wiping cloth in question was discarded in the trash. If hands need to be wiped then they should be properly washed prior to using a clean paper towel to dry hands.
Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment. Employees working in dish room must properly wash their hands after handing soiled utensils/equipment and prior to handling clean utensils/equipment. Common towels are prohibited. Towels used with sani-buckets can not be used for wiping hands unless it is a fresh cloth that is immediately discarded in the trash after use.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text:
750.830 - Dish machine sanitizer concentration was at 0ppm chlorine. Manager primed the line and after running a few more cycles the sanitizer concentration was 100ppm. All racks of dishes that just went through the machine were to be placed through an entire cycle again to ensure proper cleaning and sanitizing of dishes. Use of test strips and general dish machine maintenance were discussed. Check the sanitizer concentration the first run of the day and periodically throughout the day to ensure sanitizer and other chemicals are dispensing properly. 
All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text: 750.810 - Wet wiping cloths were observed on counters and carts outside of solution at different times during the inspection. Wiping cloths are to be stored in the sanitizer solution between uses to inhibit the growth of microorganisms. Maintain solutions at 100ppm and store wiping cloths properly. if wiping cloths are no longer needed then discard the wiping cloths in the trash.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - Butter cups that were placed out on tables at lunch time had internal temperatures of 55F-68F. Label on containers state "Keep Refrigerated; Store at 35F-45F". Cook noted the butter cups were probably out for ~1hr prior to being placed back in the cooler. All butter cups with internal temperatures above 45F were voluntarily discarded in the trash. Maintain cold potentially hazardous foods (PHF) at 41F/below. If butter cups are placed on tables during dining hours they can not be placed back in the cooler for later use. Time control must be applied and all butter cups would need to be used or discarded w/in 4hrs. Otherwise, get out a few butter cups at a time and supply more as residents request them in order to maintain product at 41F/below in the cooler.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment: 750.140b - Pans of peas, stuffing, and pork were observed cooling at room temperature. Pans were sitting on a counter, covered with foil. Internal temperatures of peas and stuffing were 112F and 123F respectively. Pork was at 134F-140F. Ice baths were made for all three foods and temperatures were monitored during inspection. Foil was removed to allow heat to vent off of cooling foods. Internal temperatures of products began to drop, and cook was advised to continue monitoring the foods throughout the cooling process. Cooked PHF shall be properly cooled from 135F to 70F w/in 2 hrs and from 70F to 41F/below w/in an additional 4 hrs. Total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs. **Educational handouts on cooling and calibrating stem thermometers were provided.**.(see general comments)

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text: 750.810 - Buckets of sanitizer solution were not at 100ppm chlorine. One bucket tested at 0ppm. Two other buckets tested at +200ppm and less than 100ppm after recently being remade. All buckets were made to be at proper concentration of 100ppm. Maintain sanitizing solutions at 100ppm; change solutions every 2 to 4 hours or more often if solutions and wiping cloths become heavily soiled. Store wiping cloths in the sanitizer solutions between uses.
